first.rationale: Activation is down 6% QoQ, the most pressing metric. memory_91 demonstrated that activation messaging inside the product improved week-one engagement. memory_86 showed onboarding simplification lifted early adoption. Both address the activation gap directly. Verifying memory_91 confirms the messaging approach still applies; verifying memory_86 ensures we understand the relationship between onboarding completion and activation outcomes. Activation_messaging is lower risk than promotional_pricing (which could devalue the product against competitor pressure without solving activation) and doesn't require established customer base like referral_incentive. It directly addresses the 6% activation decline while preserving our pricing strategy integrity and avoiding unsustainable acquisition tactics. A standard_experiment scope allows measured validation before broader rollout.

final.rationale: Verification confirms both prior experiments. exp_91 showed in-product activation messaging delivered +6% activation and +11% week-one engagement with +1% retention lift. exp_86 showed shortened onboarding improved completion +13%, reduced time-to-value by 2.1 days, and increased 30-day retention +3%. The current 6% QoQ activation decline is the primary metric at risk. Activation_messaging directly addresses this gap based on proven prior performance. Unlike promotional_pricing (which risks margin against competitor pressure without solving activation), this preserves pricing strategy while improving the product experience. This is lower risk than enterprise_sales_assist (which requires longer sales cycles) given we need immediate sustainable impact. Standard_experiment scale allows measured validation. Combining with insights from memory_86 and memory_31, we can layer messaging improvements with any onboarding optimizations. This maximizes qualified revenue by improving activation efficiency rather than discounting.
